name: MACHHLI
title: Queen of Ranthambore / Crocodile Hunter
territory_zone: Lake Palace, Rajbagh, Malik Talao, Ranthambore Fort
death_cause: Natural death due to extreme old age at 20 years in Amareshwar forest range
significance: The most famous tigress in recorded history. Credited with single-handedly generating over M in tourism revenue for Rajasthan. Fought and killed a 14-foot Mugger Crocodile in a 4-hour mortal duel in 2003, losing teeth in the process. Lived to an unprecedented 20 years, far exceeding the normal 12-14 year wild lifespan. Received the TOFT Lifetime Achievement Award.

name: CHARGER
title: The Supreme Monarch of Bandhavgarh

lineage.consort: Sita (Legendary Bandhavgarh Tigress / NatGeo cover star)

territory_zone: Tala Core Zone, Chakradhara, Bandhavgarh Fort foothills
death_cause: Old age and injuries sustained after being pushed to the park boundary by younger rivals
significance: The tiger who made Bandhavgarh world-famous. Earned his name because he aggressively mock-charged tourist jeeps and elephants to assert absolute sovereignty. Reigned as supreme ruler of Tala for over a decade alongside Sita. Given a formal state forest cremation and monument at Charger Point in Magdhi/Tala upon his death in 2000.

name: MUNNA
title: The Walking Legend of Kanha
territory_zone: Kanha Meadows, Mukki, Kisli, Khatia buffer
death_cause: Old age, translocated to Bhopal Van Vihar in 2019 after territory loss, passed away in 2021
significance: Renowned across global wildlife photography for the distinct black stripes on his forehead that naturally read "CAT" and "PM". Ruled Kanha meadows with absolute authority for over 12 years. Fearless walker who often marched directly down the safari tracks for kilometers without breaking stride.

name: COLLARWALI
title: Supermom of Pench / Mataram

lineage.offspring: World Record 29 cubs across 8 successful litters (25 survived to adulthood)

territory_zone: Karmajhiri, Touria, Pench River banks, Alikatta
death_cause: Natural death due to old age and multiple organ failure on 15 Jan 2022
significance: The Mother of Pench. World-record holder for the highest number of cubs birthed by any wild tiger in history (29 cubs). First tiger radio-collared in Pench as a subadult in 2008 by WII. Single-handedly repopulated Pench and revived tiger densities across Central India. Given full state honors and public traditional floral funeral by forest staff and local villagers.

name: WAGDOH
title: The Colossus of Tadoba / Scarface
territory_zone: Moharli Buffer & Moharli Core
death_cause: Dead due to extreme old age, natural
significance: One of the largest, heaviest male tigers ever recorded in Central India (estimated 250+ kg). Famous for the deep gash across his right eye earned in territorial battle with Yeda Anna. Ruled the Telia Lake basin for nearly a decade, fathering over 40 cubs including the legendary Telia Sisters. Even in his late teens, his sheer bone density and massive skull intimidated every younger rival.

name: BAJRANG
title: The Warlord of Moharli
territory_zone: Moharli Core, Junona Buffer, Dewada, Agarzari, Telia Lake
death_cause: Killed in an epic territorial clash with younger male Chhota Matka in Chandrapur buffer forest
significance: The most dominant and territorial fighter in Tadoba for over a decade. Possessed an unusually muscular frame and fought constantly to expand his domain from core into buffers. Fathered dozens of cubs with multiple core matriarchs. Died as a warrior on 18 Nov 2023 in an intense claw-to-claw territorial war against Chhota Matka.

name: JAI
title: The Great Wanderer / Sultan of Umred
territory_zone: Nagzira WLS -> 150km corridor migration -> Umred Karhandla WLS, Paoni range
death_cause: Mysterious disappearance in April 2016; presumed killed or poisoned along migration corridor
significance: The iconic six-foot-tall, 250 kg colossus who famously walked over 150 km across highways, canals, and human settlements from Nagzira to Umred Karhandla in 2013, single-handedly turning UKWLS into a premier tiger sanctuary. His radio collar went silent in April 2016, sparking India’s largest-ever wildlife search operation.

name: T-24 USTAD
title: The Sultan of Ranthambore
territory_zone: Zone 1, Zone 2, Zone 6, Singhdwar, Sultanpur, Kala Peela Dhand
death_cause: Bone cancer and chronic respiratory distress at Sajjangarh Biological Park, Udaipur (28 Dec 2022)
significance: The most controversial and formidable tiger in Indian history. Reigned over Ranthambore’s rocky gorges with terrifying power. In May 2015, following the death of forest guard Rampal Saini, he was controversially declared a man-eater and translocated to Sajjangarh Biological Park under immense public protests and Supreme Court petitions. Subject of the award-winning documentary "Tiger 24" by Warren Pereira.

name: BHEEM
title: The Mountain Titan of Bandhavgarh
territory_zone: Khitauli Core, Magdhi, Mirchahani range
death_cause: Severe territorial combat injuries with younger rival males in Khitauli range
significance: Inherited the legendary genetics of B2 and Charger. Possessed exceptional shoulder height, heavy neck scruff, and a devastating swipe force. Reigned supreme over the rocky sandstone cliffs of Khitauli, driving out multiple intruding males and safeguarding generations of cubs.

name: MATKASUR
title: The Sovereign of Telia Lake
territory_zone: Telia Lake, Moharli Core, Tadoba Lake basin
death_cause: Fatal territorial clash with younger male rivals near Moharli buffer
significance: Named for his round "matka-like" belly and deep throat rumble. Replaced Wagdoh as the supreme master of the Telia Lake waters and sired Tadoba’s most powerful modern dynasty, including current dominant male Chhota Matka and Tarachand. Renowned for his patient ambush hunting tactics in the high grasslands.

name: YEDA ANNA
title: The Phantom of Kolsa / Crooked Tail
territory_zone: Moharli Core, Kolsa, Katezari, Jamni
death_cause: Injuries sustained in historic territorial war with Wagdoh and subsequent displacement
significance: Instantly recognizable by his distinct crook at the tip of his tail. Preceded Wagdoh as the monarch of Moharli. Fought Wagdoh in a legendary clash that left Wagdoh with his permanent scarface. Sired Chhoti Tara, who went on to become one of Tadoba’s greatest founding matriarchs.

name: GABBAR
title: The Iron Fighter of Agarzari
territory_zone: Agarzari Buffer, Moharli Core borders, Dewada
death_cause: Severe territorial combat trauma during the intense triangular war for Tadoba core
significance: Nicknamed "Leopard Face" for the dense rosette-like spot patterns near his whisker pads. Known for an aggressive, uncompromising temperament. Fought continuous multi-front wars against Saturn and Tyson to control the gateway between Tadoba core and the southern buffer corridors.

name: KHALI
title: The Giant of Agarzari
territory_zone: Agarzari Buffer, Junona, Dewada-Adegaon buffer
death_cause: Territorial battle injuries and natural physical decline in July 2021
significance: Carried forward the colossal genetic bulk of Wagdoh. Reigned as the undisputed giant of the Agarzari and Junona buffers. Tourists and naturalists marvelled at his massive head circumference and fearless disposition. Sired several litters with the W-Mark female.

name: SHIVA
title: The Kolsa Titan
territory_zone: Zari, Kolsa Core, Shivanzhari, Pangadi
death_cause: Territorial combat and old age displacement in the rugged southern Kolsa ranges
significance: Brother of Khali and direct son of Wagdoh. Migrated deep into the southern wilderness of Kolsa and established an impregnable stronghold across Zari and Shivanzhari. Sired the formidable Yuvraj (T-164) and maintained genetic dominance across the buffer boundary.

name: SAMRAT
title: The Noble Challenger
territory_zone: Moharli Core, Khutwanda, Navegaon boundary
death_cause: Fatal injuries sustained in a vicious mating battle against dominant male Mowgli (July 2019)
significance: A majestic, broad-chested tiger who dominated the central Moharli trails. Engaged in one of the most violent recorded battles in Tadoba history against Mowgli in July 2019 over mating rights with the Mayuri female, succumbing to mortal wounds after fighting to the bitter end.

name: NEERA
title: The Matriarch of Pandharpauni / Mother of Maya
territory_zone: Pandharpauni Meadow, Tadoba Lake shore, Jamunbodi
death_cause: Tragic early demise in 2012 caused by venomous snake bite while defending cubs
significance: The biological mother of Maya, Tadoba’s most iconic modern tigress. Ruled the prime grasslands of Pandharpauni. Her tragic death in 2012 orphaned Maya and her siblings at a tender age, forcing Maya to fight for survival and eventually rise to become the Queen of Tadoba.

name: NARSIMHA
title: The Phantom Prowler of Kolsa
territory_zone: Kolsa Core, Zari buffer, Bori trail
death_cause: Displaced in fierce multi-male territorial conflict and natural mortality in deep Kolsa
significance: Known for his stealth and exceptional nocturnal hunting skills. Ruled the heavily forested hills of Kolsa, holding off intruding males from Chandrapur borders with fierce scent-marking patrols.

name: NATRAJ
title: The Sovereign of Zaripeth
territory_zone: Zaripeth Zone, Pangadi Buffer, Kolsa South
death_cause: Defeated in brutal combat by Jr. Mowgli in Zaripeth buffer in late 2022 / early 2023
significance: The undisputed master of the Zaripeth and Pangadi buffer corridors. Documented extensively by Onkar Bhople in the Tadoba Territorial Directory. Fought gallantly against younger rising males before yielding the Zaripeth throne to Jr. Mowgli.

name: KATEZARI / TYSON
title: The Heavyweight Boxer of Katezari
territory_zone: Katezari valley, Jamni, Tadoba Core centre
death_cause: Injuries and exhaustion resulting from the multi-year triangular core territorial warfare
significance: Named "Tyson" for his sheer fighting aggression and tendency to box with both front forepaws during duels. Turned the Katezari and Tadoba core into an active battlefield in the early 2010s alongside Saturn and Gabbar, keeping Bajrang pushed south toward Telia.

name: MADHURI
title: The Telia Matriarch / Queen of Queens

offspring: The Telia Sisters (Sonam T-24, Lara T-19, Geeta, Monstrous Telia Litter)

territory_zone: Telia Lake basin, Agarzari, Moharli Buffer
death_cause: Natural death due to old age in the Agarzari buffer zone
significance: The single most influential tigress in Tadoba’s history. Together with Wagdoh, she created the immortal Telia dynasty. Her daughters—the four Telia Sisters (Sonam, Lara, Geeta, and their sister)—dominated Tadoba’s central tourism for over a decade. Mother of Khali and Shiva.

name: TARACHAND
title: The Prince of Jamni Lake
territory_zone: Jamni Lake, Tadoba Core, Navegaon buffer
death_cause: Fatal territorial skirmish during early adulthood dispersal
significance: Brother of Chhota Matka, born to the powerhouse union of Matkasur and Chhoti Tara at Jamni Lake. Beloved by tourists and photographers for his gentle yet bold curiosity around safari vehicles before his tragic early demise.

name: RAAVAN / KANKAZHARI
title: The Ten-Headed Warlord of Kolara
territory_zone: Kankazhari, Kolara Buffer, Palasgaon boundary
death_cause: Territorial battle injuries and natural mortality in Kolara buffer (2023)
significance: Feared across northern Tadoba for his massive muscular frame and ruthless boundary defense. Kept younger dispersing males like Joga Moga completely out of Kolara buffer for nearly a decade. Re-sighted after a full year in 2021 on night safaris looking battle-hardened and sovereign.

name: SATURN / NAMDEV
title: The Ringed Monarch / Core Sentinel
territory_zone: Tadoba Core Centre, Khatoda, Katezari Road
death_cause: Old age and territorial combat wounds during the core supremacy clashes
significance: One of the tri-rulers who locked the Tadoba Core into an impenetrable triangle with Tyson and Gabbar. Famous for distinct circular ring stripes on his tail and flanks, earning him the moniker "Saturn".

name: SHIVAJI
title: The Great Chhatrapati of Tadoba
territory_zone: Moharli Core, Khutwanda, Vasant Bhandara
death_cause: Natural death following territorial displacement by Bajrang and younger titans
significance: Named after the legendary Maratha warrior king Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Reigned with immense dignity and calm poise across the historic trails of Moharli before the rise of the younger generation. His bold strolls down the main tar road of Moharli are legendary.

name: CHHOTA MUNNA
title: The Prince of Mukki
territory_zone: Mukki Core, Sondhar Meadow, Babathenga
death_cause: Territorial battle injuries sustained in Mukki range in 2023
significance: True heir to Munna’s throne. Inherited his father’s immense length, heavy swagger, and territorial aggression. Ruled Mukki range for nearly 8 years, holding off younger dispersers from Balaghat corridors.

name: UMARPANI MALE
title: The Ghost of Kanha Highlands
territory_zone: Umarpani Plateau, Kisli Core, Kanha Valley
death_cause: Natural death due to old age and hunting limitations in Kisli hills
significance: A massive highland male who ruled the remote Umarpani plateau. Mastered ambush predation on Gaur (Indian Bison) along the steep escarpments, maintaining an aura of quiet invincibility.

name: BAISANGHAT MALE
title: The Meadow King of Sarhi
territory_zone: Baisanghat, Sarhi Core, Silpura corridor
death_cause: Old age and territorial clash with younger Kisli males in late 2019
significance: The largest male tiger documented in Kanha’s northern Sarhi and Baisanghat ranges. Known for massive paws and a deep, resonant territorial call that could be heard across entire mountain valleys.

name: SURYA
title: The Sun Monarch of Bandhavgarh
territory_zone: Tala Core, Mirchahani, Sehra Meadow
death_cause: Natural death and territorial skirmish trauma in Tala rocky gorge (2022)
significance: Golden-coated monarch of Bandhavgarh. Sired critical litters with Kankati and ruled the Tala core with calm, fearless authority, completing the generational line from Charger and B2.
